items.note: The prompt mentions about 2 million rows and says memory grows with the export.
It requires keeping the signature `export_orders_csv(db, path)` and notes that three callers use it.
It requires the exact header and column order, though the header string itself is invented.
It says "Don't add any dependency" and to ask first if one seems needed, which matches the rule.
It names the N+1 per-row customer lookup as the known main cause.
It says to write rows to the file as they are produced instead of building one big string.
It says customer names can contain commas and need proper CSV quoting with the csv module.
It says to run the existing tests in tests/test_export.py without editing them.
It asks for a minimal, targeted change and says not to restructure the module.

invented: The full current source of export_orders_csv is shown, including its exact queries, string building and file write. Neither the request nor the answers provided it.
The exact customer query `SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id = ?` and the orders query with columns id, customer_id, total_cents, created_at.
The current number formatting (`total_cents/100:.2f`, `created_at.isoformat()`) and '\n' line endings in the old output.
The claim that the old code would crash when an order's customer_id has no matching customer.
